title: Coordinate routine releases from an authorized workflow start
statement: The system shall coordinate preparation, qualification, publication, public verification and reporting for eligible reviewed release input from one authorized workflow start, without a subsequent routine human approval, while stopping for failed checks, unsupported decisions or unavailable prerequisites.

what.problem: A nominally automated release can still require copying identities across files or manually coordinating every helper and result.
what.desired_outcome: A maintainer initiates the authorized release operation and receives its actual result without a second confirmation or manual stage coordination.

why.rationale: Existing routine coordination promises remove repeated manual bookkeeping without removing engineering decisions, evidence, or publication authority.

conditions: For a release eligible under the existing adopted routine automation path.

contexts: The bounded release coordinator and its existing preparation, validation, publication, observation, and reporting owners.

how.approach: Bind release authority to the initiating source, supported configuration and execution path. Derive profiles, notes and evidence from reviewed inputs, qualify and retain the resulting packages, then publish and observe them automatically. Stop on failed checks or unsupported decisions; never replace a candidate during a retry or interpret a passing local check as authority.

how_much.scope: Supported routine releases only. No new general workflow engine, public CLI command or optional approval mode. Credentials and source protection remain setup prerequisites. A future additional approval gate requires a separate requirement decision.

acceptance_criteria: An eligible authorized workflow start progresses through qualification to publication and reporting without a second human approval or manual profile/hash entry.
Failed or incomplete qualification prevents publication even though the workflow start was authorized.
Source, version, configuration and destinations are bound to initiation; the exact resulting checked packages are retained for publication and retry.
A local check, PR validation run or unrelated workflow start grants no publication authority.
Retries inspect public state and reuse the original candidate; changed material scope requires a new authorized start and qualification, not silent substitution.
Ambiguous version intent, unsupported special handling or unavailable prerequisites produces a precise intervention request.
